title: Choose the visual direction for the Axia approval and denial workspace
question: Every option shows the screen admins use most: held rebates on the left, one rebate open with its approval conditions and the Approve / Decline actions. Colors, Poppins and the left sidebar stay fixed; composition, density and one signature move change. Pick one, or ask for another hand.

options.label: Funding Statement
options.lineage: Bank remittance advice and funding statements
options.thesis: Each rebate decision is footed like a statement: every approval condition is a line item, and the result is the total.
options.viewport: Sidebar left; a week strip that ties out (submitted = auto-approved + held + declined); held rebates as statement lines with amounts right-aligned; the open rebate as a stub listing proof of purchase, CRM install status, PTO, campaign dates, serial file and integrity checks, footed to Approve or Hold.
options.risk: Money framing must not crowd out the reason a rebate was held; reasons lead every line.

raised.raise: Review mode: one held rebate owns the work area and the next one is already loaded, one keystroke away.
One body size across every table; rank is carried by weight, rules and reversal, not by size steps.
Structure comes from strong rules on one sheet, not from floating cards.
Every record leads with its reference number as its identity: tracking number, invoice number.
Conflicts such as duplicate claims are drawn as a crossing mark, so they read without relying on color.

options.label: Permission to Operate
options.lineage: Utility interconnection and PTO approval letters
options.thesis: Each rebate decision reads like a utility approval letter: numbered conditions, each satisfied or not, and an outcome line.
materials: an approval line that reads like a stamp
options.viewport: Sidebar left; a compact held-rebate list on the left; the open rebate on the right as a letter: reference block, conditions 1 to 10 with satisfied marks, outcome line and the Approve / Decline actions at the foot.
options.risk: The letter form can slow scanning across many rebates; it is strongest on the single-rebate view.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: Boarding pass and live gate board
options.thesis: The queue is a live board ranked by age; a rebate whose state changes stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: Sidebar left; held rebates as a live board in fixed columns ordered by wait time, newly held rows lit teal until opened; the open rebate below as a segmented pass with its conditions.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: held rebates map to departures and the lit change state helps monitoring; ops staff do not recognize travel, so it loses on identification.
options.risk: Ranking by age can hide high-value or high-risk rebates unless a second sort is obvious.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the screen; the next is one flick away.
options.viewport: One rebate fills the screen with actions stacked on the right.
options.case: Loses both: staff need comparison across rebates, and the feed hides the queue.
options.kept: Review mode keeps the next held rebate loaded one keystroke away.
options.risk: Removes the overview that monitoring depends on.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and rule.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides along a lit bed.
options.case: Loses both: raked layouts and goldenrod light fight the fixed palette and a working screen.
options.kept: Tables use one body size and carry rank with weight and rules.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: A printed sheet registered by crosshairs and hairlines.
options.viewport: One continuous sheet of plates and credits.
options.case: Loses both: gallery framing and faint hairlines conflict with the request for clearly visible sections.
options.kept: Structure from strong rules on one sheet instead of floating cards.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact is a numbered catalog entry.
options.viewport: A black field with a fac number as the headline.
options.case: Loses both: black ground and coded labels break the palette and plain-language status.
options.kept: Records lead with their reference numbers as identity.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over a zone ramp; crossing hatches mark conflict.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets on a backlit field.
options.case: Loses both: darkroom craft is foreign to solar ops, and overlapping sheets hide data.
options.kept: Duplicate-claim conflicts are drawn as a crossing mark, readable without color.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean admin dashboard of the kind every SaaS ships, executed at full craft in the Axia palette.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, metric tiles, then the held-rebate table with a detail drawer.
canonCard.risk: This is the generic SaaS look you said would feel wrong.
